newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish leaders wish Pope speedy recovery.
newsitem.headline: Polish leaders wish Pope speedy recovery.

text.p: Poland's ex-communist prime minister, acting on behalf of millions of his compatriots, on Tuesday wished Pope John Paul a speedy recovery and looked forward to his planned visit to his homeland next year.

"In the name of millions of Poles, my government and myself, I wish to express my concern over your state of health and wish you the fastest return to that activity which has characterised the whole pontificate of Your Holiness," Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said in a letter to the Pope.

"I view with deep respect the Mission which Your Holiness fulfils for the good of mankind and the world's nations, for the shaping of coexistence between societies, founded on principles of peace and love," Cimoszewicz said.

He expressed conviction that the forthcoming 18th anniversary of the current pontificate and the 50th anniversary of John Paul's priesthood would allow the Pope to experience the respect and admiration in which he was held.
The Pope, 76, had his appendix removed on Tuesday in Rome and doctors said the operation had been a perfect success.

A spokesman for President Aleksander Kwasniewski, who is also a former communist, said the Polish leader had been following reports of the Pope's operation closely and with concern and was delighted it had gone well.

Kwasniewski was hoping that the Pope's planned visit to Poland in June next year, during which he is to attend a eucharistic conference in the western city of Wroclaw, "would be a great event for all Poles", Antoni Styrczula told Reuters.
Pope John Paul enjoys huge popularity in his overwhelmingly Catholic homeland, which his influence helped to free from communist rule in 1989.

The Catholic Church in Poland has, however, repeatedly clashed with the coalition government's dominant, secular-minded Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), to which Cimoszewicz belongs and which Kwasniewski used to lead.
Last week Church influence helped to ensure that the upper house of parliament blocked a measure liberalising the current tough anti-abortion law.
The bill, which the Pope denounced -- saying that a country which killed its own children had no future -- is now due to go back to the lower house for a hard-fought final vote.
The church is also campaigning for a new national constitution, now being drafted, to contain an invocation to God in its preamble -- an idea opposed by SLD parliamentarians.

Parliamentary elections are due in September next year and the Pope's visit could give a boost to opposition parties grouped around the deeply-Catholic Solidarity union, despite attempts by Kwasniewski to win over Catholic voters.
